questions_and_answers.question: Which of the following bonds would have the greatest percentage decrease in value if all interest rates in the economy increase by 1%? a) 1-year, 10% coupon bond. b)20-year, 5% coupon bond. c)10-year, zero coupon bond. d)20-year, zero coupon bond. e) 20-year, 10% coupon bond.
questions_and_answers.answer: The bond that would have the greatest percentage decrease in value if all interest rates in the economy increase by 1% would be the one with the longest maturity and the lowest coupon rate. This is because the value of a bond is inversely related to interest rates, and bonds with longer maturities and lower coupon rates are more sensitive to changes in interest rates. Explanation When interest rates rise, the present value of a bond's future cash flows (which are fixed) decreases, causing the bond's price to fall. This is known as interest rate risk. Two main factors affect a bond's interest rate risk: Maturity: Longer-term bonds have greater interest rate risk because their cash flows are received over a longer period of time. Therefore, a rise in interest rates has a larger impact on the present value of these cash flows.
